text:
deploy-bot: Deployed nvidia-driver 546.12 to canary h100 pool (asia-east1) at 04:12 UTC.

omar: seeing a flurry of alerts from canary transformers — lots of CUDA launch failures and OOMs. rolling back?

lia: same — pods hitting ~98% GPU memory shortly after warmup, then `CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`. No app code change.

omar: paste of a pod log: ```RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory when allocating 134217728 bytes
  File "/app/runner.py", line 232, in forward
  cudaLaunchKernel returned 2 (out of resources)
  PTX: unresolved reference to `_ZN6kernel...`
```

ops-monitor: node metrics: h100-canary-node-7 memory usage jumps before container starts JIT compile step. nvtop shows persistent resident size +1.8GB compared to previous driver.

sylvie: interesting — vendor note said 546.x changes PTX JIT behaviour for SM90 (codegen uses larger shared memory per-block in some kernels). could explain extra resident usage.

kyle: any NCCL errors? I saw a few `ncclCommInitRank` warnings but not widespread. this feels like kernel codegen -> higher per-kernel scratch.

omar: repro steps on a canary node: `docker run --gpus=all mytransformer:canary ./run_eval.sh` -> after a couple batches it OOMs, earlier driver 535.101 had stable memory.

lia: quick mitigation: can we force lazy module loading? setting `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY` reduced peak in a quick test (dev only). not a long-term fix.

ops-monitor: temporarily cordoning canary pool to stop new rolls and draining running jobs. started at 04:30 UTC.

deploy-bot: rollback request queued — rolling 546.12 back from canary pool to 535.101 now. ETA ~12m.

omar: logging an incident and collecting nvdisasm/cubin diffs for a couple failing kernels. attaching small sample: ```nvdisasm: kernel shmem usage 6144 -> 16384 (after 546.12)```

vendor-nv-team: thanks for the samples. unusual jump — could be aggressive PTX-to-cubin optimization for SM90. requesting full nvcc flags and a sample PTX for debugging.

sylvie: actionable next steps: 1) finish canary rollback 2) run smoke on all h100 pools with 535.101 pin 3) gather a representative set of failing kernels + PTX/cubin diff 4) ask vendor for a compatibility patch or opt-out flag 5) evaluate `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY` cluster-wide as a short mitigation (cost = slightly higher latency).

kyle: cost note — if we use LAZY and fallback, peak memory per worker reduces but throughput drops ~8% from our bench. will affect reserved capacity planning for Dedicated customers.

lia: created a shared folder with logs + nvdisasm samples: https://internal.redwood/infra/h100-ptx-regressions/1958420000

omar: next status update after rollback completes and canary runs smoke. for now paused any driver rollouts beyond canary.

ops-monitor: rollback finished at 04:44 UTC, canary health checks greening up. will keep pods under observation for 2 hours.

vendor-nv-team: we have a hypothesis — new CodeGen is increasing shmem for certain matmul kernels on SM90. sending a small patch to avoid the aggressive path. will share a build tomorrow.

omar: thanks — marking incident P2. follow-up: schedule an eng-infra + ML-runtime sync to decide whether to accept the vendor patch or require an opt-in flag, and update rollout guardrails.

lia: adding ops ticket to require a canary soak window + perf snapshot before driver promotion. :memo:

kyle: pinging product for customer impact / communication if we need a brief notice to Dedicated customers.

deploy-bot: Note: driver rollouts remain blocked until the new canary passes a 6-hour soak window.

omar: closing for now — keeping thread open for vendor updates and perf diffs.
